subject: System Design
title: The Byzantine Generals Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Byzantine Generals Problem.

hook.text: What if some generals are traitors who send conflicting messages? How do loyal generals still agree?

buildup.text: Byzantine fault tolerance handles nodes that lie, send wrong data, or behave maliciously.

discovery.text: You need at least 3f+1 nodes to tolerate f Byzantine faults. With 1 traitor, you need 4 generals.

twist.text: Bitcoin solved the Byzantine Generals Problem for open networks using proof of work — a breakthrough.

climax.text: Most internal systems assume crash failures, not Byzantine ones. Blockchains assume Byzantine failures everywhere.

punchline.text: Byzantine tolerance: reaching agreement despite liars.

quiz.question: How many nodes are needed to tolerate f Byzantine faults?
